name: Waldorf Astoria Orlando
positioning: Official Walt Disney World hotel within the Bonnet Creek Resort, bordered by Disney-owned land, with a Rees Jones golf course and a shuttle to the parks
best_for: Families who want Disney park perks such as early theme park entry and a park shuttle
Golfers who want an 18-hole championship course on site near the Disney parks

facts.text: Waldorf Astoria Orlando is an official Walt Disney World hotel.
The hotel runs continuous motorcoach transportation to all four Walt Disney World theme parks and Disney Springs.
Shuttle pick-up is at the hotel's porte-cochere.
Guests can purchase Lightning Lane experiences starting at 7 am Eastern, three days before their visit.
The Concierge team can assist with Disney ticket orders and theme park dining reservations.
The hotel offers a private transportation service.
The hotel is part of the Bonnet Creek Resort.
The lobby rotunda has a black-and-white marble floor and a clock tower at its center.
Bathrooms have separate walk-in showers and soaking tubs.
The pool is lined with cabanas.
Bull & Bear offers table-side preparation of steakhouse classics.
Astoria After Dark provides dinner and activities on Friday and Saturday evenings.

highlights.text: The resort is bordered by Disney-owned land on all sides.
The hotel has an 18-hole championship golf course designed by Rees Jones.
Guests get a 30-minute early entry to all four Walt Disney World theme parks.
Guests can explore the Disney parks with their own VIP Tour Guide in a customizable experience.
Disney View rooms have a view of the theme parks, and park-view rooms can catch the nightly fireworks show at Disney's Hollywood Studios.

considerations.text: The resort borders Disney-owned land but is not on Disney soil, so park visits mean taking the hotel's motorcoach shuttle or private transportation.
Theme park views come with Disney View rooms specifically.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the high-end positioning.
